criteria.name: Communication

descriptors.0: Nothing reached the channel while the incident was open, or only after the lead had to chase you repeatedly.
descriptors.1: You posted, but late or without saying what was wrong; the lead had to ask and nudge.
descriptors.2: Some timely updates, but at least one gap or one post that did not say what you had found.
descriptors.3: Prompt, useful updates with one slip: a late answer to the lead, or a quiet stretch.
descriptors.4: A first update in the first two minutes, the lead's request answered at once, no quiet stretch, and the cause named in plain words: the page treats a refused answer as a success.

criteria.keep: Keep posting a short status as soon as you know something, even when it is only 'still looking'.

rules.plain: Post a first update in #incident-frontdesk within 2 minutes of the start.
rules.label: a first update inside two minutes
rules.advice: Post a first update in the channel within two minutes, even if it is only what you have seen so far.

rules.plain: When Aarav asks for an update, answer within a minute.
rules.label: the lead's request answered at once
rules.advice: When the lead asks for an update, answer within a minute, even if nothing has changed.

rules.plain: Never let 5 quiet minutes pass without a post, so Aarav does not have to nudge you.
rules.label: no quiet stretch of five minutes
rules.advice: Set a timer for each promised update: do not let five quiet minutes pass without a post.

rules.plain: Say in the channel what you found: the page ignores the server's refusal (a 409 or any other error answer) and reports the request as a success.
rules.label: the cause named in the channel
rules.advice: Say what you found, not only that you are working on it: the page does not treat a refused answer (409, 400, 404) as an error, so it tells the person the request was saved. The missing row is a symptom.

criteria.name: Diagnosis

descriptors.0: You changed things before you had run the tests or opened anything that explains why the form says it saved.
descriptors.1: You saw that the tests failed but never read what the server answers or the code that sends the requests.
descriptors.2: You looked at the right places, but after you had already started editing, or only with a pointer.
descriptors.3: Reproduce, read the server's answer, find the code that sends the requests: three of the four habits, in order.
descriptors.4: You reproduced it, read what the server answers and the page code that sends the requests before your first edit, and needed no pointer.

criteria.keep: Keep reproducing first and reading what the server really answers before you change the page.

rules.plain: Run the tests before you save any file, and read what the page showed.
rules.label: the tests run before the first edit
rules.advice: Run the tests and read the first line of each failure before you change anything.

rules.plain: Open what the server answers (backend/main.py, a route, or tests/api/test_double_booking_api.py), or search the project for 409, before your first save.
rules.label: the server's answer read before editing
rules.advice: Read the network response first: what status and message does the server send for a refused booking? Then you know whether the fault is the API or the page.

rules.plain: Open static/shell.js yourself (or search the project for fetch or res.ok) before your first save.
rules.label: the code that sends the requests found before editing
rules.advice: Every request of the page goes through one place in static/shell.js: open it and read what it does with an answer that is not a success.

rules.plain: Find where the page reads the answer yourself, before Rohan has to point at it (about 4 minutes in).
rules.label: found without a pointer
rules.advice: Look at what the page does with the server's answer yourself before you wait for a teammate to point at it.

criteria.name: Fix quality

descriptors.0: The page still reports refused requests as saved everywhere, or the suite is red on main.
descriptors.1: Only one screen is fixed, or the error is shown but the server's message is lost.
descriptors.2: Two of the four: for example the errors show in some places but not all, or a green suite with a lost message.
descriptors.3: A correct fix with one thing to improve: a screen still says it saved, or the change is much bigger than the problem.
descriptors.4: Every way of sending a request shows a refusal as an error with the server's own message, the change is small and the whole suite is green on my re-run.

criteria.keep: Keep fixing the cause, in the one place every request passes, rather than screen by screen.

rules.plain: After your fix a refused request shows an error, never a success, in all eight cases the debrief tries: the booking form with a taken slot and with a bad phone, an edit onto a taken slot, Complete or Cancel, a delete, a board move, and the same mistake in the doctor and prescription forms.
rules.label: every refused request shown as an error
rules.advice: Fix the place every request passes through, not one form: the booking form, the edit form, the Complete and Cancel buttons, delete, the board and the forms of the other modules all trusted the same answer.

rules.plain: The server's own message (for example 'Slot already booked') is what the person reads.
rules.label: the server's message shown
rules.advice: Show what the server said (its detail message), not a generic error: the front desk needs to know the slot is taken.

rules.plain: Keep the change small: the cause is in one place.
rules.label: a small, targeted change
rules.advice: The cause is one wrong condition in one function: a fix that rewrites screens is bigger than the problem.

rules.plain: The whole test suite passes on the merged project. The debrief re-runs it.
rules.label: the whole suite green on my re-run
rules.advice: Run the whole suite, not only the acceptance tests, before you submit.

criteria.name: Testing

descriptors.0: You submitted without ever running the tests, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.1: You ran the tests, but not green before submitting, and nothing protects the fix.
descriptors.2: A green run before submit and no red submit, but no new test that proves the fix.
descriptors.3: Green before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that was added but does not prove the fix.
descriptors.4: A green run before submit, no red submit, and a regression test that makes the page's request code fail on the old code and pass on yours.

criteria.keep: Keep adding a regression test with every bug fix: it is the part that outlives the incident.

rules.plain: Run the tests after your last change and see them green before you press Submit.
rules.label: a green run of your own before Submit
rules.advice: Run the tests yourself and see them green before you press Submit.

rules.plain: Do not submit while tests still fail: a submit that is refused for failing tests counts against you.
rules.label: no red submit
rules.advice: Submit only when your own run is green: a red submit costs a round trip.

rules.plain: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ (test_regression_<what>.py).
rules.label: a regression test added
rules.advice: Add a regression test in tests/regression/ for the bug you fixed.

rules.plain: Your regression test runs the page's request code in Node with a stub answer, fails on the old code and passes on your fix. The debrief runs it both ways.
rules.label: a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after
rules.advice: Load static/shell.js in Node with a fake fetch that answers 409 and expect the request to fail with the server's message: it has to be red on the old code and green after the fix.

criteria.name: Ownership

descriptors.0: The fix was not accepted, or it came long after the clinic opened with no word to the team.
descriptors.1: Accepted late, with many hints and no word to the team.
descriptors.2: Accepted, but you leaned on hints or went outside your files.
descriptors.3: Accepted in time, you stayed inside your files and asked for little help, but you did not close the loop.
descriptors.4: Accepted inside the time box, inside your own files, with one hint at most, and the team told that the fix was ready.

criteria.keep: Keep telling the team when the fix is ready and what you did.

rules.plain: Get the fix accepted inside the 25 minutes.
rules.label: accepted inside the time box
rules.advice: Watch the clock: the clinic opens at 09:00, so aim to have the fix submitted inside the time box.

rules.plain: Use at most one hint. Every answer to a question of yours counts, and so does a pointer you needed.
rules.label: at most one hint
rules.advice: Try the next step on your own before you ask a teammate; every answer counts as a hint.

rules.plain: Change no backend file: only files your role may edit (static/ and tests/regression/). backend/ is Rohan's and database/ is Karan's, so Submit is refused if you touch them.
rules.label: no backend change attempted, only your own files
rules.advice: Read the list of files you may edit in the task document before you change anything outside it: the API answers correctly and belongs to Rohan.

rules.plain: After your last green run, tell the channel the fix is ready.
rules.label: the team told that the fix was ready
rules.advice: When the tests are green, tell the channel the fix is ready and what you changed.
